maria: Quick recap — I ran a canary that turns on aggressive KV prefetch at admission to avoid page-fault stalls during batch formation. Latency numbers look better (p50 ~12% lower, p95 ~6% lower) but we hit sporadic OOMs when queue depth spikes. Causing nodes to drop requests.

sam: Can you paste the profiler snippets and which kernels are touching the KV buffers?

maria: pasted profiler excerpt below — main points: prefetch path allocates GPU KV buffer before kernel select, kernel set includes `matmul_fused_v2`, `attention_kv_prefetch`. Observed memory delta ~+40MB per prefetched request on average during seq_len=128 runs.

```
Profile @ shard-2 2026-03-18T15:04
- matmul_fused_v2: p50 9.1ms p95 18.6ms
- attention_kv_prefetch: p50 2.4ms (allocs ~40MB)
- total batch assemble: p50 18ms p95 65ms
memory: free 12.3GB -> 11.2GB after 6 concurrent prefetches
```

lee: if we're preallocating 40MB per request, queue depth >5 will chew >200MB just on prefetch. That plus other allocations explains the OOMs. Are we prefetching at admission or just before kernel launch?

maria: at admission — we wanted continuous batches to start execution without stalls. Current admission allows queue depth up to 8 (legacy). When depth hits 6+, OOMs become common on smaller cards.

ton y: idea: gate prefetch with a dynamic headroom estimator and a token-budget target. Something like: headroom = free_mem - reserved_margin; prefetch_cost_est = avg_prefetch_bytes_per_request; token_budget = floor(headroom / avg_kv_bytes_per_token); only prefetch if token_budget >= min_tokens_for_prefetch else disable prefetch for that request and fall back to CPU-side KV fetch.

sam: that makes sense. Do we have a reliable avg_kv_bytes_per_token number?

maria: from the recent run: conservative avg_kv_bytes_per_token ~= 70KB (includes quantization metadata & alignment). That leads to ~9MB per 128-token sequence, but the prefetch path also includes buffer padding and per-request overhead so we saw ~40MB empirically. We should use a rolling 1h p95 to be safe.

lee: admission policy change proposal (short):
- probe GPU free memory at admission (fast ioctl)
- compute prefetch_allowed = free_mem > (prefetch_est + safety_margin)
- if prefetch_allowed -> do admission + prefetch; else -> admit but mark `no_prefetch` and enqueue to cpu-kv-fallback queue
- add fast bailout in batcher: if aggregate_prefetch_est > headroom then stop admitting new prefetching requests and start forming "no-prefetch" sub-batches.

maria: I'll prototype a `prefetch.safety_margin` flag and `prefetch.min_headroom` + `prefetch.fallback=cpu` config. Plan: canary on shard-0 with seq_len workloads 64/128/512 next week.

ton y: pseudocode for the estimator — can someone sanity-check?

```
function allow_prefetch(free_mem):
  headroom = max(free_mem - reserved_margin, 0)
  per_req = max(rolling_p95_prefetch_est, static_prefetch_floor)
  if headroom < per_req + safety_margin:
    return false
  # token budget heuristic
  token_budget = floor(headroom / avg_kv_bytes_per_token)
  return token_budget >= min_tokens_for_prefetch
```

sam: looks good. Add a short circuit to check gpu_peak_allocs in last 10s to avoid flapping.

lee: also add a quick probe hook in the kernel selector so that if a prefetch would change which kernel we pick (due to memory layout) we recalc.

maria: action items: (1) I prototype config + estimator by Friday, (2) sam adds perf suite for seq_len 64/128/512 to measure p50/p95 and memory deltas, (3) lee adds GPU mem probe hook and fast aggregate estimator, (4) canary on shard-0 next Tue.
